title: Tokyo dark — Autumnal Equinox Day, falling on the US 5-Year note and 2Y FRN auctions the day after the 2-Year
source: EST: jpx.co.jp/english/corporate/about-jpx/calendar/index.html (Market Holidays, the page's own 'Update : Feb. 06, 2026'), fetched direct 2026-09-15 (HTTP 200, 33,103 bytes) — the 2026 panel reads verbatim 'Sep. 23 (Wed.) Autumnal Equinox', third in the run 'Sep. 21 (Mon.) Respect for the Aged Day', 'Sep. 22 (Tue.) Holiday 2', under the page's standing rule 'JPX markets are closed on Saturdays, Sundays, national holidays, and on the dates indicated below.' Corroborated at a second, independent primary in the same session: Japan's Cabinet Office national-holiday file www8.cao.go.jp/chosei/shukujitsu/syukujitsu.csv (HTTP 200, 21,538 bytes, Shift-JIS), whose 2026 rows read 2026/9/21 敬老の日, 2026/9/22 休日, 2026/9/23 秋分の日. Note the date is NOT a fixed calendar date in statute — Autumnal Equinox Day tracks the astronomical equinox and is fixed for each year by cabinet ordinance on the National Astronomical Observatory's determination — which is exactly why it is taken from the published 2026 calendars above rather than derived. Stays estimate on the two standing counts the sibling jpx-market-closure entries already record, neither of them date doubt: market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for a securities exchange's own holiday calendar, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-15
notes: PROPOSED during the treasury-2y-note-2026-09-22 adjacency sweep (2026-09-15, D-7), the third session of a five-session JPX blackout (Sat 2026-09-19 through Wed 2026-09-23, the longest run in Japan's 2026 calendar). It matters to this corridor because 09-23 carries BOTH treasury-5y-note-2026-09-23 and treasury-2y-frn-2026-09-23 — and the 5-Year is the tenor whose soft indirect share (61.5%, 2026-08-26, -2.6pp against its own prior-11 mean) is the standing weak leg this calendar tracks, so the temptation to explain its next print with 'Tokyo was shut' is real and specific. MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: it would be the wrong explanation. Across 1,108 Treasury note/bond auctions since 2016 (Fiscal Data auctions_query, shares over competitive accepted, pulled direct 2026-09-15), the 37 held on a Japanese national holiday drew mean indirect 63.35% vs 61.89% on Tokyo-open days — the wrong sign for the hunch, Welch t=+0.850; dealer takedown 20.87% vs 23.52%, t=-1.412. On 2-Year notes alone (n=171): dark 55.22% (n=9) vs open 55.44% (n=162), t=-0.050. Inside three-plus-session blackouts (n=15 auctions): 60.57% vs 61.89%. The 2025-09-23 2-Year auction was itself held on Autumnal Equinox Day and printed indirect 57.7% / dealer 11.5%, both on its own norm. Impact low: no Japan-listed symbol is tracked here and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is rates- or Tokyo-keyed. One genuine second-order note, flagged not claimed: boj-decision-2026-09-18 lands the last Tokyo session before the blackout opens, so whatever the BoJ sets has three dark days to sit before Japanese accounts can act on it in size — an observation about sequencing, with no measured price channel behind it. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
